newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary milling wheat prices jump on quality fears.
newsitem.headline: Hungary milling wheat prices jump on quality fears.

text.p: Milling wheat futures prices on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) continued to rise on Thursday on fears of a low-quality crop, dealers said.
"There is widespread market talk that the wheat crop, while good in volume terms, would be of lower quality," said Dezso Kormendi of brokerage LaSalle.

These worries as well as a somewhat rosier export outlook drove milling wheat prices higher over the last week and after three consecutive limit-up rises the daily 400 forints per tonne price change barrier was removed.

This allowed January milling wheat to jump 930 forints to settle at 24,550 forints, slightly below a trading high of 24,600 forints, while March closed at 25,300 forints, up 600, but down from the day's peak of 25,700 forints.
All other milling wheat positions went limit-up.
Kormendi said that while quality worries drove up milling wheat prices, feed wheat went limit-down for all positions for the very same reason.

Maize futures rose by between 30 and 320 forints for all but July. Kormendi said the rise could be explained by a slow reaction to earlier Chicago price rises but it was more likely due to general market sentiment dominated by rising milling wheat prices.
The day's total grains turnover of 1,090 lots or 498 million forints was little changed from Wednesday's 1,089 lots or 493.3 million forints.
Milling wheat accounted for most of the turnover in volume terms with 810 lots.
